metadata.rustBuild: cargo build --locked --release --target wasm32-wasip1 (opt-level=3, thin LTO, codegen-units=1, strip=true)

methodology.runtime: Node/V8; identical synchronous benchmark host, WASI shim, linear-memory ABI, SQL protocol, model and sorted snapshot bytes
methodology.guest: One hydrated phase-2 ABI call; pre-encoded input. Includes guest JSON parsing, model/CEL validation, tuple validation/indexing and resolution; output decoding included. Excludes host SQL and input encoding.
methodology.sqlite: Complete two-call Check inside an existing SQLite in-memory transaction; includes SQL preparation/reads and host JSON encoding/decoding. Excludes fixture setup and transaction begin/commit/rollback.
methodology.statistics: Median of per-process medians across fresh processes. p95 is median of process p95 values. Process order alternates. Every response is checked. Warmups and iteration counts are recorded. No persistent guest authorization caches.
methodology.startup: Fresh-process WebAssembly.compile and instantiate+_initialize; excludes artifact I/O, process launch and network. V8 may defer optimization to warmup. First SQLite Check is reported separately after schema setup, before any model/check warmup.
methodology.memory: Max observed linear memory across all workloads, and peak RSS of a complete worker process (includes Node/V8/SQLite/JIT). Neither is per-check allocation.
methodology.limitations: Rust is an experimental independent evaluator with a conservative scalar CEL subset and restricted numeric-string conversion; passing tested corpora is not full OpenFGA or CEL conformance. Results compare these two ports, including differing validation/telemetry/runtime designs, rather than Go versus Rust universally. One local machine; no remote database/network or durable commit costs measured.
methodology.snapshotAdapter: Source inspection: Go hydrates each snapshot through upstream MemoryBackend.Write, whose insertion loop scans previously accumulated records for every tuple (pkg/storage/memory/memory.go:391). It also creates ULIDs and change records. Rust builds an indexed read view. The large-snapshot comparison therefore includes a quadratic Go adapter cost; it is not an isolated graph-algorithm or language speed comparison. No CPU profile was taken to assign percentages to individual costs.

gate.tests: 516 upstream assertions, 21 shared cases, 100 Hegel histories per artifact, transaction failure/isolation checks, all generated benchmark workloads
